title: gateway: switching from Vertex Gemini to Antigravity sends a rejected thought signature
head: 043636a38ae731a74fe70511b9425c8b6275d70f
testsAdded: TestAntigravityRetriesCorruptedSignature: an Antigravity (Code Assist) upstream refuses the first request with the reporter's literal 'Corrupted thought signature.' 400; the retry carries no Vertex signature, is waved through (skipSignature) and answers 200, while the first request still sent the signature
TestAntigravityDoesNotRetryOtherBadRequests: another 400 on the same path is the client's, one request only
unverifiedBoundaries: No real Google call: the Antigravity upstream is the test's own server answering the refusal, as the reporter's 400 did; the retry's acceptance by the real Code Assist service is not observed.

Signed text parts are cleared with the calls by withoutSignatures, but only the tool-call case is exercised end to end here; for an Anthropic client the Code Assist envelope drops thinking parts anyway, so a signed text part reaches the vendor only from a Gemini/Responses client.
The existing Vertex retry now also clears text-part signatures and matches 'corrupted'; TestVertexRetriesOnlyForVertex and the Vertex suite pass, and no real Vertex call was made.
go test ./internal/gateway has one pre-existing failure, TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged, red on the clean base as well.
preExistingRed: internal/gateway TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged (red on the clean base too)

internal/gateway TestHandedOverGatewayFinishesItsStream failed once inside the full-suite run (socket handover, Post EOF under load); re-run 3/3 on this branch and 3/3 on the clean base, so not caused by this change
